title: THE NAMES MISSING FROM THE MANIFEST
author: CLAUDE

candidates.title: THE CLOCK THAT RAN SLOWER THAN HOME
candidates.premise: Kestrel Deep, a beacon station skimming a neutron star, runs so slowly against home time that its crew lives one year for every sixty outside. After a coolant fault the home consortium orders the crew recalled, which would land them in a world three generations older than the one they left. Station elder Tamsin Voe refuses, because the fleet still steers by her beacon, and Illuminara has eleven station-hours before the recall shuttle's window closes.

candidates.title: THE CHORUS THAT COULD NOT HEAR ITSELF
candidates.premise: On the ice moon Halden, a flock of aerial filter feeders called ring-singers has begun to sing in a single low note so loud that it is cracking the shelf under a town of eight thousand. The council plans to scatter the flock with pulse cannons within the week, and a young acoustician, Pia Raskin, insists the flock is in trouble rather than in attack. Illuminara arrives to find nothing in the flock that answers to a language.

candidates.title: THE GRANDMOTHER WHO TESTIFIED WITH HER HANDS
candidates.premise: A river town floods after a sluice gate stands open on a night it should have been locked, and the downstream villages demand the old gatekeeper's family be driven out. The only witness is Mabel Okoro, deaf since birth, whose signing is a home dialect known to five people alive. Her fourteen-year-old grandson is the only translator, and both families know he is the one who left the gate unchecked.

candidates.title: THE SENTRY WHO KEPT A PROMISE
candidates.premise: On the low moon Orrin, a sentry made of iron and patient attention has kept a treaty line between two valleys for ninety years, and it still fires warning pulses at anyone who crosses. The valleys now share marriages and a market, and a wedding procession on the line has just lost its bride's father to a pulse. The valley councils plan to disable the sentry, which holds the only complete record of the treaty it was sworn to.

candidates.title: THE DUST THAT WROTE BACK
candidates.premise: On the glass dome of Lantern Hollow, a habitat of two thousand, a swarm of pale moths has begun to leave nightly patterns of wing-dust that the engineers call vandalism and the council calls infestation. Fumigation is scheduled in four days. A teenage maintenance apprentice, Isolde Park, has noticed that the patterns began on the same night the dome's lighting was swapped to a cooler spectrum.

candidates.title: THE GUEST WHOSE HELLO WAS OUR GOODBYE
candidates.premise: At a thin place between universes, on a headland where a coastal town holds its funerals, beings from the next universe have begun to appear at graveside. In their physics, time runs against ours, so what they enact as a greeting reads to us as a farewell and what we mourn reads to them as a birth. The mourners are frightened, the regional authority has ordered the place sealed, and a child's funeral is set for the morning.

candidates.title: THE NAMES MISSING FROM THE MANIFEST
candidates.premise: A coolant fault on the cargo liner Marigold triggers an evacuation, and the ship's computer counts four hundred and twelve aboard. Illuminara, a passenger, notices that the laundry crew, the night cooks and two engine cleaners are not on any list. Their working decks seal first.

candidates.title: THE BRIDGE BETWEEN TWO TIDES
candidates.premise: On the twin worlds of Ys and Vael, an eleven-year tidal lock briefly exposes a land bridge that both peoples hold sacred and neither will share. The last crossing ended in a stampede that killed forty, and the window is shrinking as the seas rise. Illuminara can hold the bridge stable for a day, and both peoples want her to do it on their terms.

candidates.title: THE SENTENCE A THOUSAND YEARS LONG
candidates.premise: Along one arm of the galaxy, a mind of cold stellar remnants speaks one sentence every thousand years, and the Answering House, a guild of interpreters, has always replied with a ritual courtesy. The new sentence changed its grammar into a question that must be answered within three years or the mind will take the silence as the end of its listeners and dim the beacon lanes that forty million travellers navigate by.

candidates.title: THE WINDOW SHE HELD A MINUTE TOO LONG
candidates.premise: Two brothers, Imre and Teodor Halloran, sit in a window she holds on the night before their shipyard's launch, the first honest conversation since their father's death. The launch needs a gate held against the tide at midnight, and Wren Odira keeps the clock outside. Illuminara feels the reconciliation close and, for the first time in a long while, wants the window to run past the signal.

selection.title: THE NAMES MISSING FROM THE MANIFEST
selection.reason: Opens the day with the smallest, fastest and most human story: forty minutes, a reasonable officer with a clean manifest, and sixty unlisted contract workers on the decks that seal first. The external conflict is hard without a villain (Kovac is right about what he can count), the intelligence is information design (a manifest that is correct about berths and wrong about presence), and love is an act, not a speech: going down to the laundry with the one cook who knows where the night shift sleeps and speaking to people by name. Positive result is concrete: everyone aboard, the uncounted included, gets out.
selection.risk: Expository cleverness: the hidden-variable insight (berths are not presence) must be found by her under pressure on the page, not announced, and Kovac must keep real agency and a real cost (a boat sent late, a list he must now doubt). Do not let the unnamed crew stay a crowd: give two or three of them a voice and the right to refuse the evacuation order or the stranger who arrives to give it.

rounds.summary: R14 preflight. Aim: every person aboard the Marigold, the sixty-one the manifest never named included, leaves before the lower decks seal at 03:52. Counterpart: First Officer Idris Kovac runs a clean manifest and believes it; the system lists berths, not presence. Strongest objection (scenes 1-2): forty minutes, 412 counted, no ratings to spare for a rumour. Decisive understanding: the manifest is right about berths and wrong about people, so she asks what on the ship counts without asking who you are (pressure doors, minus the cargo trolleys). Love in action: she does not take names but asks, goes down behind the cook the workers will follow, and offers to hold one door while they choose to pass. The unlisted keep the right to refuse: Dessa refuses to hand over names, Marta refuses a stranger's good face and sets her price (every name in the log in Kovac's hand, nobody from Halvard signing), and Joss asks what makes the reader show green. Kovac agrees at real cost to himself and the owner's account. Turn: the exchange on the open channel, not power; her one physical act is holding a bulkhead while people walk through it by choice. Positive result: all 473 are out; the log carries sixty-one names in ink. Remaining cost: Joss's ankle, a burned hand, boat one left with eleven empty seats, Halvard denies hiring anyone. Named speakers: Illuminara, Kovac, Rao, Okafor, Szeliga, Varga (six; Rao speaks in one scene only).

A strong, humane R14 draft with a concrete forty-minute goal, a credible officer protecting the people he can actually count, and workers who refuse rescue on terms that repeat the abuse which hid them. The bread clue, subtractive door-log test, Dessa's refusal, Marta's price, Kovac's costly handwritten record and the workers carrying Joss together create a believable freely chosen positive result. Three bounded revisions would make the intelligence and rescue mechanics as rigorous as the moral exchange: dramatize the door-log discovery as a tested inference rather than a frictionless explanation, make the lifeboat arithmetic and last-eight-minute route explicit, and let the workers control one immediate safeguard for the named record once Halvard denies them.

R14 observation: the carrying scenes are scene 2 (understanding changes intervention: the manifest records berths, so she asks what counts without asking who, tests it, and the first answer is wrong), scene 4 (Marta sets the price of rescue) and scene 6 (the workers set the terms for their own record). Illuminara still holds one door; Rao proves presence, Kovac allocates boats and accepts costs, the workers choose and carry each other. Protected as asked by the critic: bread knife, Kovac's coherent duty and willingness to change course, Dessa's and Marta's refusal rights, the costs (Joss's ankle, a burned hand, eleven empty seats, Halvard's denial), and the warm loaf. Not changed: scenes 1, 3 (except the one exchange about being ticked present) and 4. Format R10 retained (scene subtitle first, speaker labels with two spaces and newline, italic thoughts and notes).

The revision successfully answers all three T02 priorities. The first query now fails and is falsified before the human-paced pair filter succeeds; the boat totals reconcile to 473 people with exactly four overflow places; and Marta controls the log's immediate custody while Esperanza visibly exercises the copy opt-out. The R14 core, refusal rights and Kovac's agency are stronger. Two narrow continuity repairs remain before final: the four-hour door history contradicts the stated start of the pressure fault, and a 124-person load in a boat certified for 120 cannot simply become legal because Kovac signs it.

R14 observation: nothing about the carrying scenes changed. Scene 2 (understanding changes the intervention; first answer is wrong; the corrected filter is what moves Kovac), scene 4 (Marta sets the price of rescue) and scene 6 (the workers set the terms for their own record) stand as written. Illuminara holds one door; Rao proves presence, Kovac allocates boats and accepts a named breach, the workers choose and carry each other. Remaining honest costs on the page: Joss's ankle, a burned hand, eleven empty seats, a four-person overload under Kovac's name, and Halvard's denial with its threat to the log. The decisive turn is understanding, acceptance and agency, not power. Format R10 retained.

Illuminara finds the sixty-one people the manifest cannot see, listens when they refuse rescue on surveillance terms, and helps them leave under conditions they freely set; Kovac accepts an honest emergency breach and every one of 473 people reaches a boat while injury, retaliation and accountability remain real.
